fixes.explanation: There's no silver in this verse. Esther 4:4 says the queen was overcome with distress and sent clothes for Mordecai to wear instead of his sackcloth. Mordecai had put on sackcloth and ashes and gone out wailing loudly and bitterly (Esther 4:1). I think Esther saw a man in mourning clothes and wanted to put him in something else. Her gift answers his sackcloth, not his address.

Not in this verse, friend. Esther 4:4 says the queen was overcome with distress and sent clothes for Mordecai to wear instead of his sackcloth. Mordecai had gone out wailing loudly and bitterly (Esther 4:1), and he wouldn't accept the clothes. I think she wanted to ease his grief, not send him away. A message would have been words, but she sent something he could put on.

The officials aren't part of her plan. They do show up earlier in her message, when she says all the royal officials know the law about approaching the king uninvited (Esther 4:11). In her plan she asks for a fast from the Jews in Susa, and she joins it with her maidens. Maidens fills the blank, friend.
